title: The Vimose inscriptions — earliest datable Elder Futhark runic texts
language_note: Early Proto-Norse / late Proto-Germanic, written in the Elder Futhark runic alphabet — the earliest attested Scandinavian writing system, emerging during the period of intensive Roman-era contact (possibly influenced by contact with Mediterranean/Roman-provincial alphabets, though the exact model is debated).
date: c. 160-300 CE (Roman Iron Age in Scandinavia)
findspot: Vimose bog, island of Funen (Fyn), Denmark — a wetland weapon-deposit site

findspot_places.name: Vimose
findspot_places.note: Confirmed against the Pleiades places snapshot of 2026-08-10 by coordinate — 55.460, 10.180, island of Funen — feature type 'settlement', attested -30..300, which matches the deposit horizon. A search for 'Fyn' returned only 'Asfynis' in Egypt, a substring coincidence: the site name resolves, the modern island name does not.

original_text_note: Transliterations per the Kiel Runenprojekt database as summarized on Wikipedia; readings for several items remain debated among runologists. RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-10: this field previously read as an English catalogue listing with the runic text embedded in it — 'Vimose Comb (c. 160 CE, oldest known datable runic inscription): harja ...' — so the retrieval index held the cataloguer's English prose labelled as Proto-Norse source text, and a Part 7 citation of it would have quoted a museum label as if it were an inscription. The Part 3 fidelity classifier passed it because catalogue prose contains few English function words, so english_marker_ratio stayed under threshold; the Part 6 translation check caught it downstream instead, when the model correctly declined to translate an English list and handed it straight back (chrF 0.981 against the source, flagged untranslated_echo). The field now holds the transliterated runic text only, one object per line. Object identification, dates and the comb's runic characters moved to `notes` and `object_sequence`, where they are documentation rather than something retrieval can mistake for a source.
reference_translation: harja: likely a personal name or 'comb'/'warrior'. mariha ... makija: possibly 'Mari (the famous one) is the sword of Alla'. awgns: possibly 'son/descendant of Awa'. Several inscriptions remain only partially deciphered.
translation_source: Kiel Runenprojekt (runenprojekt.uni-kiel.de) interpretive database, as summarized on Wikipedia (Vimose inscriptions).
notes: Vimose is a weapon-sacrifice bog deposit containing Roman-influenced military equipment alongside the earliest Scandinavian writing — making it the clearest Scandinavian case where a genuinely regional-language text (proto-Norse runes, not Latin or Greek) and direct Roman-contact material culture come from the very same findspot and period. High-value candidate for the hero cross-lingual demo, notwithstanding that many individual readings are short and contested. Object identification for original_text_excerpt, in line order: (1) Vimose Comb, c. 160 CE, harja, runes ᚺᚨᚱᛃᚨ, the oldest known datable runic inscription; (2) Vimose Buckle, c. 200 CE; (3) Vimose Chape, c. 250 CE; (4) Vimose Woodplane, c. 300 CE; (5) Vimose Sheathplate, c. 300 CE; (6) Vimose Spearhead. Moved out of the original-text field 2026-08-10 — see original_text_note.
